newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bank ex-official arrested in IBM probe.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bank ex-official arrested in IBM probe.

text.p: A former board member of Argentina's state-run Banco Nacion turned himself in to police after a judge ordered his arrest in connection with an alleged bribery case involving International Business Machines Corp's local unit.

Alfredo Aldaco surrendered late Wednesday after Judge Adolfo Bagnasco issued arrest warrants for him, former Nacion head Aldo Dadone, two former IBM Argentina officials and a former government official. The others are not in custody.
The judge suspects bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure IBM won a $250 million contract to install a computer system at Banco Nacion.
Bagnasco said in his ruling Tuesday that "the market price of products and services accepted by Banco Nacion was about 50 percent lower than that charged by IBM Argentina SA."

Among those under warrant for arrest were former IBM Argentina head Ricardo Martorana and his deputy Gustavo Soriani. The judge said the five had engaged in bribery, while Dadone and Aldaco were also accused of embezzling public funds. Five others were indicted in connection with the case.

Dadone and Aldaco, among others indicted, "accepted from those who were then the top responsibles for IBM Argentina SA -- Ricardo Martorana and Gustavo Soriani -- the promise to give them an undetermined amount of money in order to arrange the award of the tender...to that company," the judge said. "All signs indicate the tender was tailor-made for IBM."

At the heart of the probe are payments made to IBM's subcontractor CCR, which according to Bagnasco "benefited from a $37 million deal" he suspects went to alleged bribes. The judges believes CCR was used as a funnel for the alleged illegal payments.
CCR was in charge of providing a backup computer system not included in the tender. Bagnasco said CCR was a small firm with no infrastucture and only one employee.
The judge has asked U.S. authorities to hand him information on a Citicorp account in New York where money from CCR was transferred. He is also probing other banks' accounts.

The judge has traced CCR's deposits for about $9 million in an account of a Banque Bruxelles Lambert SA bank branch in Geneva. At his request, the Swiss supreme court lifted banking secrecy in August.
IBM Argentina has denied any wrongdoing, although it has admitted to errors "inconsistent with company policy."

Banco Nacion last year canceled the deal and sued IBM Argentina for $174 million, accusing it in a Buenos Aires Administrative Contentious Court, which arbitrates commercial disputes, of not complying with deadlines. IBM countersued for $86 million, alleging "wrongful revocation" of the contract.
Other IBM Argentina deals are the subject of separate probes.
